summary: Backend-only regression + confirmation testing of new X-API-Key-authenticated user management endpoints: POST /api/user-create, /api/user-update, /api/user-deactivate. Created dedicated pytest file /app/backend/tests/test_user_mgmt_apikey.py with 21 tests covering happy paths, all documented error cases, envelope shape, auth scoping (Bearer rejected on API-key endpoints), deactivate->login=403->reactivate flow, and regression on /api/user-auth. All 21 tests pass (100%). Test data cleaned up (0 leftover TEST_ users, 0 leftover TEST_ api_clients). Super Admin untouched.
critical_code_review_comments: routes_mobile_auth.py user_update: field _normalize_optionals filters None but keeps is_active=False (correct via explicit is_active pass-through). Verified via test_is_active_toggle.
user_update returns 400 'No fields to update' if no non-None payload fields—reasonable but not in the spec; not surfaced as an issue.

user_update _validate_role_office is called with updates.get('role_id') / updates.get('office_id') which may both be None on partial updates (e.g. only name change); ensure that helper is a no-op when both are None to avoid inadvertent validation failure. Current tests pass, so behavior is fine, but worth a defensive assertion.

user-create audit log stores raw request payload including password when present; password IS excluded because it's not in `data` (password is hashed into `pw_hash` and only doc fields pass through). Confirmed safe.
test_credentials: Admin: sa@bprbangunarta.co.id / SA@4dm1n. Default user password: bpr2026. API key minted per-run via POST /api/clients and deleted in teardown.
seed_data_creation: Per-test users created with email prefix `TEST_um_<random>@example.com`; API client name prefix `TEST_apiclient_<random>`. All cleaned up in module-scoped teardown fixtures. Verified 0 leftover artifacts after full run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with: `ADMIN_EMAIL=sa@bprbangunarta.co.id ADMIN_PASSWORD='SA@4dm1n' REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> pytest backend/tests/test_user_mgmt_apikey.py`. The shared /app/backend/tests/conftest.py auto-injects an admin Bearer token on ALL requests; the middleware in server.py checks X-API-Key first, so API-key tests still function correctly even with the Bearer header present (X-API-Key takes precedence). If server behavior changes so Bearer beats X-API-Key, the fixtures would need to strip Authorization for apikey requests.
verified_flows: POST /api/user-create success 201 envelope {success:true, data:{user, office, device}}
POST /api/user-create default password (bpr2026) applied when omitted; created user can login
POST /api/user-create duplicate email -> 409 envelope 'User email already exists' (message includes 'exist')
POST /api/user-create unknown role_id -> 400 envelope 'Role not found'
POST /api/user-create with admin Bearer only -> 401 envelope (API-key scope required)
POST /api/user-update locate by email, update name -> 200 envelope with updated profile
POST /api/user-update unknown user -> 404 envelope 'User not found'
POST /api/user-update with admin Bearer only -> 401 envelope
POST /api/user-deactivate with admin Bearer only -> 401 envelope
Regression: /api/user-auth still returns 200 envelope with user data for created users using default password
rca of the issue: N/A - no bugs found. All expected behaviors validated.
